ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: John’s miraculous birth from an elderly father and infertile mother undermines the claim that a miraculous birth proves Jesus’ divinity; John claimed no divinity and was not made a god by others.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: if a mere miraculous birth is enough to prove the divinity of Jesus (sws), then this proof is also present in favour of John (sws)

BURSEVI:v5p242/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p242/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p242/r1.claim: God only opens the door of supplication to answer it wholly or partly; opening it is a sign that mercy's doors are opening because supplication displays need and humility, which God loves.
BURSEVI:v5p242/r1.anchor: لا يمكن العبد من الدعاء إلا لإجابته كلا أو بعضا كما وقع لزكريا

BURSEVI:v5p242/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p242/r2.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
BURSEVI:v5p242/r2.claim: A report says that whoever is granted access to supplication has the doors of mercy opened.
BURSEVI:v5p242/r2.anchor: وفي الحديثك : "من فتح له باب الدعاء فتحت له أبواب الرحمة"

BURSEVI:v5p242/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p242/r3.speaker: أبو يزيد البسطامي
BURSEVI:v5p242/r3.claim: After thirty years of worship, Abu Yazid says he was told that reaching God requires poverty, helplessness, and need rather than more worship.
BURSEVI:v5p242/r3.anchor: كابدت العبادة ثلاثين سنة فرأيت قائلا يقول لي : يا أبا يزيد خزائنه مملوءة من العبادات

BURSEVI:v5p242/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p242/r4.speaker: بعض أهل المعرفة
BURSEVI:v5p242/r4.claim: A gnostic calls supplication the best weapon, fidelity the best mount, and weeping the best intercessor.
BURSEVI:v5p242/r4.anchor: نعم السلاح الدعاء ، ونعم المطية الوفاء ، ونعم الشفيع البكاء

BURSEVI:v5p242/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p242/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p242/r5.claim: The perfected seek religious rather than worldly ends; Zakariyya asks for an heir of knowledge because worldly order depends on knowledge, action, piety, justice, and fairness.
BURSEVI:v5p242/r5.anchor: ثم إن الدعاء إما للدين أو للدنيا والأول مطمح نظر الكمل ألا ترى أن زكريا طلب

BURSEVI:v5p242/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p242/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p242/r6.claim: The perfect person of each age manifests divine lights and secrets; a seeker reaches God through such a person, and should ask for the best child whose remembrance endures to the Day of Calling.
BURSEVI:v5p242/r6.anchor: وجعل الإنسان الكامل في كل عصر مجلى أنواره ومظهر أسراره فمن أراد الوصول إلى الله

BURSEVI:v5p242/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p242/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p242/r7.claim: The call to Zakariyya and glad tidings are grammatically introduced as the angel's speech; the same angelic call appears while Zakariyya is praying in the sanctuary.
BURSEVI:v5p242/r7.anchor: يا زكريا} على إرادة القول أي : قال تعالى على لسان الملك يا زكريا كما قال في سورة آل عمران

BURSEVI:v5p244/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p244/r7.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
BURSEVI:v5p244/r7.claim: The inward reading sees honors in God calling him by name, naming John before birth, and giving him a unique name in form and meaning; John never desired or intended sin.
BURSEVI:v5p244/r7.anchor: منها : أنه تعالى ناداه باسمه زكريا وهذه كرامة منه. ومنها : أنه سماه يحيى ولم يجعل له

BURSEVI:v5p244/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p244/r8.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
BURSEVI:v5p244/r8.claim: The reading says God inspires each person's name before creation, as Jesus announced a later messenger named Ahmad.
BURSEVI:v5p244/r8.anchor: إشارة إلى أنه تعالى يتولى تسمية كل إنسان قبل خلقه وما سمي أحد إلا بإلهام الله

ALUSI-FULL:v16p65/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p65/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p65/r1.claim: The address is introduced as speech delivered through an angel, who conveys the divine wording for the Prophet to recount, as in the command to say My servants.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p65/r1.anchor: لكن لا بأن يخاطبه سبحانه وتعالى بذلك بالذات بل بواسطة الملك

ALUSI-FULL:v16p65/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p65/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p65/r2.claim: The glad tidings answer Zakariya’s call and promise its fulfillment; the delay does not conflict with a prompt response, since the promise itself may count as fulfillment.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p65/r2.anchor: وهذا جواب لندائه عليه السلام ووعد بإجابة دعائه

ALUSI-FULL:v16p65/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p65/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p65/r3.claim: The common account has the announcement shortly after the prayer and birth within months; other reports place birth forty or sixty years later.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p65/r3.anchor: والمشهور أن هذا القول كان إثر الدعاء ولم يكن بين البشارة والولادة إلا أشهر

ALUSI-FULL:v16p65/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p65/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p65/r4.claim: Ghulām means a male child, though the feminine ghulāma is also used.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p65/r4.anchor: والغلام الولد الذكر وقد يقال للأنثى : غلامة

ALUSI-FULL:v16p65#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p65#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p65#2/r1.claim: Naming Yahya reinforces the promise and honors him; Ibn Abbas, Qatada, al-Suddi, and Ibn Aslam say no one before bore the same name.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p65#2/r1.anchor: وفي تعيين اسمه عليه السلام تأكيد للوعد وتشريف له عليه السلام

ALUSI-FULL:v16p65#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p65#2/r2.speaker: الزمخشري
ALUSI-FULL:v16p65#2/r2.claim: Al-Zamakhshari says rare names were favored because they attract notice and stand out; a poem praises unusual names, and Salt ibn Ata cited his foreign name among traits that advanced him.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p65#2/r2.anchor: وهذا كما قال الزمخشري شاهد على أن الأسماء النادرة التي لا يكاد الناس يستعملونها

ALUSI-FULL:v16p65#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p65#2/r3.speaker: مجاهد
ALUSI-FULL:v16p65#2/r3.claim: Mujahid, Ata, and Ibn Jubayr take samiyyan to mean equal or similar: Yahya had no equal because he neither sinned nor even intended sin.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p65#2/r3.anchor: عن مجاهد أن ( سميا ) بمعنى شبيها

ALUSI-FULL:v16p65#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p65#2/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v16p65#2/r4.claim: The Prophet says every descendant of Adam erred or intended error except Yahya, who neither intended nor committed sin; Alusi says reports on this are numerous.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p65#2/r4.anchor: عن ابن عباس أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال : ما من أحد من ولد آدم

ALUSI-FULL:v16p65#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p65#2/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p65#2/r5.claim: Other explanations say Yahya had no equal because he was born to an old man and a barren old woman, or because he embodied the qualities named elsewhere: confirmer, leader, chaste, and righteous prophet.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p65#2/r5.anchor: وقيل : لم يكن له شبيه لذلك ولأنه ولد بين شيخ فان وعجوز عاقر

ALUSI-FULL:v16p65#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p65#2/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p65#2/r6.claim: The Quranic question whether God has a namesake supports the counterpart sense; Alusi’s strongest view is that Yahya is a foreign name because Arabs did not typically name children with Arabic words.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p65#2/r6.anchor: ومن هذا الإطلاق قوله تعالى : ( هل تعلم له سميا ) لأنه الذي يقتضيه التفريع

ALUSI-FULL:v16p65#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p65#2/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p65#2/r7.claim: If Arabic, Yahya derives from a verb; proposed meanings include long life, revival of his mother’s womb, life between aged parents, wisdom, guidance, or martyrdom, since martyrs live.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p65#2/r7.anchor: وقيل : سمي بذلك لأنه حي به رحم أمه وقيل لأنه حي بين شيخ فان وعجوز عاقر

ALUSI-FULL:v16p65#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p65#2/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p65#2/r8.claim: The name may signal the inheritance Zakariya requested; Arabic and foreign derivations differ in meter and diminutive form.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p65#2/r8.anchor: وكان في ذلك إشارة إلى أنه عليه السلام يرث حسبما سأل زكريا عليه السلام

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p219#2/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p219#2/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p219#2/r1.claim: An omitted narrative clause means God answered Zachariah's prayer and announced the good news.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p219#2/r1.anchor: قوله عز وجل: {يا زكريا إنا نبشرك} وفيه اختصار، معناه: فاستجاب الله دعاءه فقال: يا زكريا إنا نبشرك،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p219#2/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p219#2/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p219#2/r2.claim: The announced ghulām is a male child.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p219#2/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p219#2/r3.speaker: قتادة والكلبي
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p219#2/r3.claim: They say no one had previously been named Yaḥyā.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p219#2/r3.anchor: قال قتادة والكلبي: لم يسم أحد قبله يحيى (5)

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p219#2/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p219#2/r4.speaker: سعيد بن جبير وعطاء
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p219#2/r4.claim: They interpret samiyyan as someone like or equal to him, as in Qur'an 19:65.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p219#2/r4.anchor: وقال سعيد بن جبير وعطاء: لم نجعل له شبها ومثلا كما قال الله تعالى: "هل تعلم له سميا" أي مثلا.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p219#2/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p219#2/r5.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p219#2/r5.claim: The intended uniqueness is that he had no equal because he never sinned or even intended sin.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p219#2/r5.anchor: والمعنى: أنه لم يكن له مثل، لأنه لم يعص ولم يهم بمعصية قط.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p219#2/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p219#2/r6.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p219#2/r6.claim: Another view says he had no equal regarding women, since he was a chief and celibate.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p219#2/r6.anchor: وقيل: لم يكن له مثل في أمر النساء، لأنه كان سيدا وحصورا.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p219#2/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p219#2/r7.speaker: علي بن أبي طلحة عن ابن عباس
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p219#2/r7.claim: No barren woman had given birth to a child like him.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p219#2/r7.anchor: وقال علي بن أبي طلحة عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما: أي لم تلد العواقر مثله ولدا.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p219#2/r8.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p219#2/r8.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p219#2/r8.claim: The statement does not give Yaḥyā every excellence, since Abraham and Moses preceded him and were superior.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p219#2/r8.anchor: وقيل: لم يرد الله به اجتماع الفضائل كلها ليحيى، إنما أراد بعضها، لأن الخليل والكليم كانا قبله، وهما أفضل منه.

BAYDAWI-FULL:19:7/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:19:7/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:19:7/r1.claim: The announcement answers Zachariah's prayer; God names the boy Yahya Himself as an honor to him.
BAYDAWI-FULL:19:7/r1.anchor: جواب لندائه ووعد بإجابة دعائه وإنما تولى تسميته تشريفا له

BAYDAWI-FULL:19:7/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:19:7/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:19:7/r2.claim: No one was previously named Yahya, showing that unusual names can ennoble the person named.
BAYDAWI-FULL:19:7/r2.anchor: وهو شاهد بأن التسمية بالأسامي الغريبة

BAYDAWI-FULL:19:7/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:19:7/r3.speaker: قيل
BAYDAWI-FULL:19:7/r3.claim: “Namesake” may mean someone comparable, as in the verse asking whether one knows any namesake of God.

BAYDAWI-FULL:19:7/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:19:7/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:19:7/r4.claim: The name is most likely foreign; if Arabic, it derives from a verb like yaʿīsh or yaʿmal. Another explanation links it to his mother's womb being revived, or God's religion being revived through his preaching.
BAYDAWI-FULL:19:7/r4.anchor: والأظهر أنه أعجمي وإن كان عربيا فمنقول عن فعل كيعيش ويعمل

QASHANI:19:5-7/r5.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:19:5-7/r5.speaker: author
QASHANI:19:5-7/r5.claim: The promised boy is the heart, named Yahya because it lives eternally.
QASHANI:19:5-7/r5.anchor: { نبشرك بغلام } القلب { اسمه يحيى } لحياته أبدا

QASHANI:19:5-7/r6.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:19:5-7/r6.speaker: author
QASHANI:19:5-7/r6.claim: Zachariah seeks a sign by which he can reach the promised heart.
QASHANI:19:5-7/r6.anchor: { رب اجعل لي آية } أتوصل بها إليه

QASHANI:19:5-7/r7.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:19:5-7/r7.speaker: author
QASHANI:19:5-7/r7.claim: Silence means not addressing sensory people with sensory preoccupations or natural affairs.
QASHANI:19:5-7/r7.anchor: { آيتك ألا تكلم } ناس الحواس بالشواغل الحسية والمخالطة بالأمور الطبيعية

QASHANI:19:5-7/r8.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:19:5-7/r8.speaker: author
QASHANI:19:5-7/r8.claim: The faculties should persist in their distinct worship through discipline and abandoning excess.
QASHANI:19:5-7/r8.anchor: كونوا على عبادتكم المخصوصة بكل واحد منكم بالرياضة وترك الفضول دائما

QASHANI:19:5-7/r9.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:19:5-7/r9.speaker: author
QASHANI:19:5-7/r9.claim: Yahya is the heart, commanded to take the book of knowledge, called the discriminating intellect.
QASHANI:19:5-7/r9.anchor: { يا يحيى } القلب { خذ } كتاب العلم، المسمى بالعقل الفرقاني

QASHANI:19:5-7/r10.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:19:5-7/r10.speaker: author
QASHANI:19:5-7/r10.claim: The heart receives wisdom while newly born in the spiritual sense.
QASHANI:19:5-7/r10.anchor: { وآتيناه الحكم } أي: الحكمة { صبيا } قريب العهد بالولادة المعنوية

QASHANI:19:5-7/r11.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:19:5-7/r11.speaker: author
QASHANI:19:5-7/r11.claim: Divine compassion is perfection through attribute manifestations; purity is sanctification through detachment.
QASHANI:19:5-7/r11.anchor: { وحنانا من لدنا } أي: رحمة بكمال تجليات الصفات { وزكاة } أي: تقدسا وطهارة بالتجرد

QASHANI:19:5-7/r12.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:19:5-7/r12.speaker: author
QASHANI:19:5-7/r12.claim: Piety avoids soul traits, and Yahya's parents are the spirit and soul.
QASHANI:19:5-7/r12.anchor: { وكان تقيا } مجتنبا صفات النفس { وبرا بوالديه } الروح والنفس

QASHANI:19:5-7/r13.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:19:5-7/r13.speaker: author
QASHANI:19:5-7/r13.claim: Peace means freedom from material entanglement; birth and death signify manifestation and annihilation in unity.
QASHANI:19:5-7/r13.anchor: { وسلام عليه } أي: تنزه وتقدس عن ملابسة المواد { يوم ولد ويوم يموت } بالفناء في الوحدة

QASHANI:19:5-7/r14.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:19:5-7/r14.speaker: author
QASHANI:19:5-7/r14.claim: Resurrection is life in God after annihilation.
QASHANI:19:5-7/r14.anchor: { ويوم يبعث } بالبقاء بعد الفناء { حيا } بالله

BIQAI-FULL:v4p522/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p522/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p522/r4.claim: God answers his prayer with a glad announcement; the doubled form of the verb, used by all except Hamza, better emphasizes news so extraordinary it might be denied.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p522/r4.anchor: وقراءة الجماعة غير حمزة بالتشديد أوفق من قراءة حمزة للتأكيد

BIQAI-FULL:v4p522/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p522/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p522/r5.claim: The child is named Yahya, a name not previously bestowed; the author says this name was reserved as an honor for him.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p522/r5.anchor: ثم وصفه بما عرف به أن مما شرفه به أن ادخر له هذا اتلاسم فقال

BIQAI-FULL:v4p522#2/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p522#2/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p522#2/r1.claim: Zakariyya asks how he can have a son and seeks confirmation, curious about the circumstances rather than doubting the truthful promise or speaking rashly.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p522#2/r1.anchor: { قال } عالما بصدقها طالبا لتأكيدها , والتلذيذ بترديدها

DURR-FULL:v5p481/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p481/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v5p481/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas interprets “no namesake before” to mean nobody had previously been named Yahya.
DURR-FULL:v5p481/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله: {لم نجعل له من قبل سميا} قال: لم يسم أحد يحيى قبله

DURR-FULL:v5p481/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p481/r2.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v5p481/r2.claim: Qatada gives the same interpretation: no one before had been named Yahya.
DURR-FULL:v5p481/r2.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله: {لم نجعل له من قبل سميا} قال: لم يسم أحد يحيى قبله

DURR-FULL:v5p481/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p481/r3.speaker: عكرمة
DURR-FULL:v5p481/r3.claim: Ikrima agrees that nobody had previously been named Yahya.
DURR-FULL:v5p481/r3.anchor: وأخرج أحمد في الزهد عن عكرمة مثله

DURR-FULL:v5p481/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p481/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v5p481/r4.claim: An alternative report from Ibn Abbas says no barren woman had previously borne a child like Yahya.
DURR-FULL:v5p481/r4.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله: {لم نجعل له من قبل سميا} قال: لم تلد العواقر مثله ولدا

DURR-FULL:v5p481/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p481/r5.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v5p481/r5.claim: Mujahid interprets “namesake” as equal or comparable.
DURR-FULL:v5p481/r5.anchor: عن مجاهد في قوله: {لم نجعل له من قبل سميا} قال: مثلا

DURR-FULL:v5p481/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p481/r6.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
DURR-FULL:v5p481/r6.claim: Sa'id ibn Jubayr glosses the word as “a likeness.”
DURR-FULL:v5p481/r6.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير في قوله: {لم نجعل له من قبل سميا} قال: شبيها

DURR-FULL:v5p481/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p481/r7.speaker: عطاء
DURR-FULL:v5p481/r7.claim: Ata gives the same interpretation as a likeness.
DURR-FULL:v5p481/r7.anchor: عبد بن حميد عن عطاء مثله

DURR-FULL:v5p481/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p481/r8.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v5p481/r8.claim: When naming a newborn Yahya, the Prophet said he would give him a name unused since Yahya son of Zakariya.
DURR-FULL:v5p481/r8.anchor: عن يحيى بن خلاد الزرقي أنه لما ولد أتى به النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فحنكه وقال: لأسمينه اسما

DURR-FULL:v5p486/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p486/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v5p486/r7.claim: In Ibn Abbas's account, Gabriel announces Yahya; his name derives from “living” and is one of God's names.
DURR-FULL:v5p486/r7.anchor: فقال: {يا زكريا إنا نبشرك بغلام اسمه يحيى} هو اسم من أسماء الله اشتق من حي

DURR-FULL:v5p486/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p486/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v5p486/r8.claim: “No namesake before” means Zakariya had no prior son and none before was named Yahya; “do you know his namesake?” means “his child.”
DURR-FULL:v5p486/r8.anchor: {لم نجعل له من قبل سميا} لم يجعل لزكريا من قبل يحيى ولد له {هل تعلم له سميا} يعني هل تعلم له ولدا

DURR-FULL:v5p486/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p486/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v5p486/r9.claim: The report links Yahya's name to Sarah: her prior name was Yisara, and the yā' was changed to ḥā'.
DURR-FULL:v5p486/r9.anchor: وكان اسمه حيا فلما وهب الله لسارة إسحق فكان اسمها يسارة

QUSHAYRI:v2p235/r1.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p235/r1.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p235/r1.claim: Yahya's name signifies life: the child will revive his barren mother, lineage, memory, and the household's worship and prophecy.
QUSHAYRI:v2p235/r1.anchor: تحيا به عقرة أمه ، ويحيا به نسبك ، يحيا به ذكرك

QUSHAYRI:v2p235/r2.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p235/r2.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p235/r2.claim: Having no namesake signals Yahya's singular excellence and lack of an equal in the totality of his virtues.
QUSHAYRI:v2p235/r2.anchor: انفراده - عليه السلام - بالتسمية يدل على انفراده بالفضيلة

QUSHAYRI:v2p235/r3.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p235/r3.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p235/r3.claim: Another interpretation says he had no peer because no one else was without sin before and after prophethood.
QUSHAYRI:v2p235/r3.anchor: لم يكن أحد لا ذنب له قبل النبوة ولا بعدها غيره

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p68#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p68#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p68#2/r1.claim: The announced speech is elliptically introduced as God's words to Zachariah; تبشير is a promise of a gift, and اسمه يحيى is a report used as a command to name him Yahya.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p68#2/r1.anchor: مقول قول محذوف دل عليه السياق عقب الدعاء

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p68#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p68#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p68#2/r2.claim: A common interpretation takes سميّا as someone with the same name before Yahya; the name's novelty honors Zachariah and makes the child easier to distinguish and a model for later naming.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p68#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p68#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p68#2/r3.claim: Ibn Ashur instead prefers سميّا as one matching Yahya in descriptive qualities: no earlier prophet combined his childhood wisdom, chastity, miraculous parentage, role announcing Jesus, and novel name.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p68#2/r3.anchor: وعندي : أن السمي هنا هو الموافق في الاسم الوصفي

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p68#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p68#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p68#2/r4.claim: Yahya's many distinctive merits do not prove he surpasses all prophets, since rank depends on the totality of merits; the maxim is that a special merit does not entail superiority.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p68#2/r4.anchor: وهي لا تقتضي أنه أفضل الأنبياء

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p5#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p5#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p5#2/r1.claim: The announcement tells Zachariah that a son named Yahya will be born to him.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p5#2/r1.anchor: المعنى قيل له بإثر دعائه يا زكريا إنا نبشرك

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p5#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p5#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p5#2/r2.claim: Most readers vocalize the verb with doubled sh; readers of Ibn Masʿud’s tradition use a still b and damma on sh.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p5#2/r2.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور «بشرك» بفتح الباء وكسر الشين

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p5#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p5#2/r3.speaker: قتادة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p5#2/r3.claim: Qatada says Yahya was named because God gave him life through prophethood and faith; another view says his guidance gave people life.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p5#2/r3.anchor: سمي يحيى لأن الله أحياه بالنبوءة والإيمان

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p5#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p5#2/r4.speaker: قتادة وابن عباس وابن أسلم والسدي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p5#2/r4.claim: They take samiyyan literally: no one had previously been given the name Yahya.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p5#2/r4.anchor: وهذا قول قتادة وابن عباس وابن أسلم والسدي

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p5#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p5#2/r5.speaker: مجاهد
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p5#2/r5.claim: Mujahid and others understand samiyyan as a peer or equal; Ibn Atiyya considers this strained unless a special distinction is intended.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p5#2/r5.anchor: وقال مجاهد وغيره سميا معناه مثلا ونظيرا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p5#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p5#2/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p5#2/r6.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas also says no barren woman had given birth to someone like Yahya.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p5#2/r6.anchor: وقال ابن عباس معناه لم تلد العواقر مثله

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p210#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p210#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p210#2/r1.claim: The narrative elides God's answer to Zakariya's prayer before the announcement of good news.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p210#2/r1.anchor: في الكلام إضمار تقديره فاستجاب الله له فقال يا زكريا إنا نبشرك

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p210#2/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p210#2/r2.speaker: حمزة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p210#2/r2.claim: He reads nubašširuka with a lightened consonant; the fuller treatment is in 3:39.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p210#2/r2.anchor: وقرأ حمزة نبشرك بالتخفيف وقد شرحنا هذا في آل عمران 39

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p210#2/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p210#2/r3.speaker: أبو صالح عن ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p210#2/r3.claim: Most authorities say no one before him was named Yaḥyā; the honor is that God named him rather than leaving his name to his parents.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p210#2/r3.anchor: لم يسم يحيى قبله رواه أبو صالح عن ابن عباس وبه قال عكرمة وقتادة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p210#2/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p210#2/r4.speaker: ابن أبي طلحة عن ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p210#2/r4.claim: A second view says no barren woman had previously borne a child like him, meaning he had no counterpart.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p210#2/r4.anchor: لم تلد العواقر مثله ولدا رواه ابن أبي طلحة عن ابن عباس

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p210#2/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p210#2/r5.speaker: مجاهد
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p210#2/r5.claim: A third view says God made him without any likeness before, since he neither disobeyed nor intended sin.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p210#2/r5.anchor: لم نجعل له من قبل مثلا وشبها قاله مجاهد فعلى هذا يكون عدم الشبه

SULAMI:v1p421#3/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p421#3/r1.speaker: الصبيح
SULAMI:v1p421#3/r1.claim: He reads Yahya's name as framed by two ya letters with the ḥāʾ of tenderness between them; the name reads in either direction, its first ya signifies divine enabling and its last verification, accounting for Yahya's sinlessness.
SULAMI:v1p421#3/r1.anchor: قال الصبيح : سماه يحيى ، وقال : ﴿ لم نجعل له من قبل سميا ﴾ افتتح اسمه بالياء وختمه بالياء

SULAMI:v1p421#3/r2.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p421#3/r2.speaker: الجنيد
SULAMI:v1p421#3/r2.claim: Yahya lives through obedience and conformity rather than dying through sin and disobedience, so he bears no mark of blame and remains praiseworthy throughout.
SULAMI:v1p421#3/r2.anchor: قال الجنيد رحمه الله : سمى يحيى ولم يكن له من قبل سميا لأن يحيى من يحيى بالطاعة

SULAMI:v1p421#3/r3.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p421#3/r3.speaker: النبي
SULAMI:v1p421#3/r3.claim: The Prophet reports that every other creature erred or intended a sin, while Yahya son of Zakariyya neither erred nor intended one; no grading is given here.
SULAMI:v1p421#3/r3.anchor: لذلك قال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم : ' ما أحد من الخلق إلا أخطأ أو هم بخطيئة إلا يحيى بن زكريا

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p214#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p214#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p214#2/r1.claim: The narrative omits the answer to Zakariya's prayer; the promise of Yahya fills it in and parallels Aal Imran.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p214#2/r1.anchor: هذا الكلام يتضمن محذوفا، وهو أنه أجيب إلى ما سأل في دعائه فقيل [له] (1) :

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p214#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p214#2/r2.speaker: قتادة وابن جريج وابن زيد
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p214#2/r2.claim: They say Yahya had no namesake before him; Ibn Jarir selects this interpretation.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p214#2/r2.anchor: قال قتادة، وابن جريج، وابن زيد: أي لم يسم أحد قبله بهذا الاسم، واختاره ابن جرير

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p214#2/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p214#2/r3.speaker: مجاهد
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p214#2/r3.claim: Mujahid interprets the phrase as saying Yahya had no counterpart or equal, using the later phrase about God's namesake.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p214#2/r3.anchor: وقال مجاهد: {لم نجعل له من قبل سميا} أي: شبيها.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p214#2/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p214#2/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p214#2/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas says no previously barren woman had given birth to someone like Yahya.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p214#2/r4.anchor: عن ابن عباس: أي لم تلد العواقر قبله مثله.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p214#2/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p214#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p214#2/r5.claim: The wording indicates Zakariya had no children and his wife had been barren from youth, unlike Abraham and Sarah, who were only old; Abraham had already fathered Ishmael thirteen years earlier.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p214#2/r5.anchor: وهذا دليل على أن زكريا عليه السلام، كان لا يولد له، وكذلك امرأته كانت عاقرا من أول عمرها،

JISHUMI:v6p4521/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4521/r8.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4521/r8.claim: The call O Zakariya has an omitted response: God answered and called to him.
JISHUMI:v6p4521/r8.anchor: يا زكريا) رفع لأنه نداء مفرد، وفي الكلام حذف أي: فاستجاب له وناداه يا زكريا

JISHUMI:v6p4521/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4521/r9.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4521/r9.claim: Samiyyan is the direct object of lam najʿal; ʿatiyyan is a specification of degree, and the nūn of takun is deleted for jussive mood.
JISHUMI:v6p4521/r9.anchor: سميا) نصب ب (لم نجعل). و(عتيا) نصب على التمييز. [(ولم تك) أصله: لم تكن] حذف النون علامة للجزم

JISHUMI:v6p4523/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4523/r3.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4523/r3.claim: God tells Zakariya that a male child named Yahya will be born; the name may promise that he will live beyond infancy.
JISHUMI:v6p4523/r3.anchor: إنا نبشرك أي: نخبرك بخبر بغلام ولد ذكر اسمه يحيى

JISHUMI:v6p4523/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4523/r4.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4523/r4.claim: Yahya's name may signify that the faith would live through him, that he revived his mother's womb, or that he never sinned; scripture calls the obedient living and the disobedient dead.
JISHUMI:v6p4523/r4.anchor: وقيل: سماه يحيى ليدل على أن الدين يحيا به؛ لأنه سأله لأجل الدين

JISHUMI:v6p4523/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4523/r5.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4523/r5.claim: The comparison with being brought from death to life is supported by the verse about one who was dead and made alive.

JISHUMI:v6p4523/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4523/r6.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4523/r6.claim: The claim that the obedient are alive is also supported by the call to what gives life and the statement that martyrs are alive.
JISHUMI:v6p4523/r6.anchor: وقال: (إذا دعاكم لما يحييكم) وقيل: سماه يحيى لأنه يقتل شهيدا والشهيد عند الله حي لقوله: (بل أحياء عند ربهم

JISHUMI:v6p4523/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4523/r7.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4523/r7.claim: Samiyyan can mean no one had been named Yahya before him, no equal, or that barren women had never borne one like him; Ibn Abbas is cited for the last reading.
JISHUMI:v6p4523/r7.anchor: قيل: لم يسم قبله أحد قبل خلقه، وإنما سمي بعد الولادة، وقيل: لم نجعل له سميا أي: نظيرا

JISHUMI:v6p4523/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4523/r8.speaker: مجاهد، سعيد بن جبير، عطاء
JISHUMI:v6p4523/r8.claim: They understand samiyyan as one without an equal or like.
JISHUMI:v6p4523/r8.anchor: وقيل: لم نجعل له من قبل مثلا، عن مجاهد، وسعيد بن جبير، وعطاء

JISHUMI:v6p4523/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4523/r9.speaker: قتادة، السدي، ابن جريج، ابن زيد، الكلبي
JISHUMI:v6p4523/r9.claim: They say no prophet before him had been named Yahya, and God honored him with an excellent name.
JISHUMI:v6p4523/r9.anchor: وقيل: لم نسم أحدا من الأنبياء قبله يحيى، وقيل: لم يسم قبله باسمه، عن قتادة، والسدي، وابن جريج، وابن زيد، والكلبي

JISHUMI:v6p4523/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4523/r10.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4523/r10.claim: The interpretation that Yahya had no inclination toward women because he was a master and continent is not convincing.
JISHUMI:v6p4523/r10.anchor: وقيل: لم يكن له ميل في أمر النساء؛ لأنه كان سيدا وحصورا، وليس بالوجه

JISHUMI:v6p4523/r11.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4523/r11.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4523/r11.claim: Muhammad was certainly later and superior; however, samiyyan need not deny every earlier prophet's excellence, and it may simply mean no one shared his name.
JISHUMI:v6p4523/r11.anchor: نقطع أنه كان بعده من هو أفضل منه وهو محمد - صلى الله عليه وسلم

JISHUMI:v6p4523/r12.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4523/r12.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4523/r12.claim: The word may refer only to a particular distinction because earlier prophets could be his equal or better; if it means the name, there is no question.
JISHUMI:v6p4523/r12.anchor: وإذا حمل على أنه خصه بهذا الاسم فلا سؤال

JISHUMI:v6p4526/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4526/r7.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4526/r7.claim: The statement that no one was named Yahya before him shows that a name may be newly assigned without earlier convention.
JISHUMI:v6p4526/r7.anchor: ويدل قوله: (لم نجعل له من قبل سميا) أنه يجوز أن يسمى الشخص باسم من غير تقدم من مواضعة

JISHUMI:v6p4526/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4526/r8.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4526/r8.claim: God's informing about Yahya before his birth shows that the nonexistent can be known.
JISHUMI:v6p4526/r8.anchor: وتدل على أن المعدوم معلوم لذلك أخبر عن يحيى وهو معدوم

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p7#2/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p7#2/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p7#2/r1.claim: No one before Yahya bore the name Yahya; the author takes this as evidence that refined, distinguished names deserve preference.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p7#2/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p7#2/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p7#2/r2.claim: The Arabs sought noble and prominent names that avoided insulting nicknames, as in the cited poem praising elegant names and red robes.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p7#2/r2.anchor: سنع الأسامي مسبلي أزر … حمر نمس الأرض بالهدب

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p7#2/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p7#2/r3.speaker: رؤبة
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p7#2/r3.claim: When the genealogist al-Bakri asked Ruʾba for his lineage, Ruʾba answered that he was the son of al-ʿAjjaj; the reply said he had understated and identified himself.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p7#2/r3.anchor: وقال رؤبة للنسابة البكري وقد سأله عن نسبه : أنا ابن العجاج

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p7#2/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p7#2/r4.speaker: مجاهد
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p7#2/r4.claim: Mujahid takes samiyyan to mean an equal or counterpart, as in the question whether one knows any namesake of God.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p7#2/r4.anchor: وقيل : مثلا وشبيها عن مجاهد ، كقوله : { هل تعلم له سميا }

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p7#2/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p7#2/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p7#2/r5.claim: If these names are Arabic, Yahya's counterparts in naming include Yaʿmar and Yaʿish; people also named a man Yamut ibn al-Mizraʿ.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p7#2/r5.anchor: ونحو : ( يحيى ) في أسمائهم ( يعمر ، ويعيش )

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p7#2/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p7#2/r6.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p7#2/r6.claim: It is also said Yahya had no equal because he never disobeyed or even intended sin, was born to an aged man and barren woman, and was chasur.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p7#2/r6.anchor: قالوا : لم يكن له مثل في أنه لم يعص ولم يهم بمعصية قط

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p356/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p356/r1.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p356/r1.claim: The annunciation comprises an answered prayer as an honor, a child as strength, and the privilege of naming him; these imply distinction and divine election.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p356/r1.anchor: فتضمنت هذه البشرى ثلاثة أشياء : أحدها : إجابة دعائه وهي كرامة .

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p356/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p356/r2.speaker: مقاتل
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p356/r2.claim: Muqatil says he was named Yaḥyā because he was born to an elderly father and an elderly mother.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p356/r2.anchor: قال مقاتل سماه يحيى لأنه صبي بين أب شيخ وأم عجوز

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p356/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p356/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p356/r3.claim: The phrase may mean no barren woman bore anyone like him, so he had no equal.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p356/r3.anchor: أحدها : أي لم تلد مثله العواقر , قاله ابن عباس .

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p356/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p356/r4.speaker: مجاهد
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p356/r4.claim: The phrase may mean Zakariya had no child before Yaḥyā.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p356/r4.anchor: الثاني : أنه لم نجعل لزكريا من قبل يحيى ولدا , قاله مجاهد .

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p356/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p356/r5.speaker: قتادة
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p356/r5.claim: The phrase may mean no one had previously been given the name Yaḥyā.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p356/r5.anchor: الثالث : أي لم يسم قبله باسمه أحد , قاله قتادة .

MUJAHID:v1p384/r1.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v1p384/r1.speaker: مجاهد
MUJAHID:v1p384/r1.claim: Mujahid glosses samiyyan as an equal or counterpart.
MUJAHID:v1p384/r1.anchor: عن ابن أبي نجيح عن مجاهد في قوله ﴿ لم نجعل له من قبل سميا ﴾ يعني مثلا

MUQATIL:19:6-8/r3.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:19:6-8/r3.speaker: author
MUQATIL:19:6-8/r3.claim: God answered Zakariya's prayer; Gabriel brought the news while Zakariya was praying, and no one before had been named Yahya.
MUQATIL:19:6-8/r3.anchor: فأتاه جبريل وهو يصلي، فقال: { يزكريآ إنا نبشرك بغلام اسمه يحيى لم نجعل له من قبل سميا }

MUQATIL:19:6-8/r4.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:19:6-8/r4.speaker: author
MUQATIL:19:6-8/r4.claim: Yahya was so named because God brought him to life through an elderly man and a barren old woman.
MUQATIL:19:6-8/r4.anchor: وإنما سماه يحيى؛ لأنه أحياه من بين شيخ كبير وعجوز عاقر.

NASAFI-FULL:v3p31#3/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p31#3/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p31#3/r1.claim: God answered Zechariah's prayer and personally named Yahya, honoring him by doing so.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p31#3/r1.anchor: تولى الله تسميته تشريفا له نبشرك بالتخفيف حمزة

NASAFI-FULL:v3p31#3/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p31#3/r2.speaker: حمزة
NASAFI-FULL:v3p31#3/r2.claim: Hamza recites يبشرك in the light form.

NASAFI-FULL:v3p31#3/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p31#3/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p31#3/r3.claim: سميا may mean that nobody before him bore the name Yahya; an unusual name merits distinction.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p31#3/r3.anchor: لم يسم أحد بيحيى قبله وهذا دليل على أن الاسم الغريب جدير بالاثرة

NASAFI-FULL:v3p31#3/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p31#3/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p31#3/r4.claim: Alternatively, سميا means peer or equal: Yahya had no equal in never sinning, being born to an elderly couple, and being ḥaṣūr.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p31#3/r4.anchor: وقيل مثلا وشبيها ولم يكن له مثل في أنه لم يعص ولم يهم بمعصية قط

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p272#5/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p272#5/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p272#5/r1.claim: Samiyyan in 19:7 means no one before Yahya had been given that name.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p272#5/r1.anchor: {لم نجعل له من قبل سميا} أي لم يسم أحد قبله: يحيى

MAJAZ:v2p2#2/r1.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v2p2#2/r1.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v2p2#2/r1.claim: يا زكريا is elliptical for فقلنا يا زكريا; the name has three forms: extended زكرياء, final-yāʾ sukūn زكريا, and زكرى like بختى.
MAJAZ:v2p2#2/r1.anchor: «يا زكريا» (7) مجازه مجاز المختصر كأنك قلت: «فقلنا يا زكريا» وفيه ثلاث لغات: زكرياء ممدود، وزكريا ساكن، وزكرى

QURTUBI-FULL:19:7-8/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:19:7-8/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:19:7-8/r1.claim: The glad tidings imply God's answer to prayer, the gift of a son, and the honor of God naming him.
QURTUBI-FULL:19:7-8/r1.anchor: فتضمنت هذه البشرى ثلاثة أشياء: أحدها: إجابة دعائه وهي كرامة.

QURTUBI-FULL:19:7-8/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:19:7-8/r2.speaker: مقاتل
QURTUBI-FULL:19:7-8/r2.claim: Muqatil says Yahya was named because he came alive between an elderly father and mother; al-Qurtubi questions this because his wife was barren, not merely old.
QURTUBI-FULL:19:7-8/r2.anchor: وقال مقاتل: سماه يحيى لأنه حيي بين أب شيخ وأم عجوز

QURTUBI-FULL:19:7-8/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:19:7-8/r3.speaker: ابن عباس وقتادة وابن أسلم والسدي
QURTUBI-FULL:19:7-8/r3.claim: They say no one had previously been named Yahya; God's naming is also a favor rather than leaving the choice to the parents.
QURTUBI-FULL:19:7-8/r3.anchor: لم نسم أحدا قبل يحيى بهذا الاسم قاله ابن عباس وقتادة وابن أسلم والسدي.

QURTUBI-FULL:19:7-8/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:19:7-8/r4.speaker: مجاهد وغيره
QURTUBI-FULL:19:7-8/r4.claim: Mujahid and others interpret samiyyan as equal or counterpart, as in 19:65; al-Qurtubi finds this far-fetched unless Yahya is uniquely distinguished in leadership or continence.
QURTUBI-FULL:19:7-8/r4.anchor: وقال مجاهد وغيره: { سميا } معناه مثلا ونظيرا،

QURTUBI-FULL:19:7-8/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:19:7-8/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:19:7-8/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas also explains that no barren woman had previously borne a child like Yahya.
QURTUBI-FULL:19:7-8/r5.anchor: وقال ابن عباس أيضا: معناه لم تلد العواقر مثله ولدا.

QURTUBI-FULL:19:7-8/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:19:7-8/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:19:7-8/r6.claim: Another view says 'before' is specified because Muhammad, who is greater, would be created after Yahya.
QURTUBI-FULL:19:7-8/r6.anchor: وقيل: إن الله تعالى اشترط القبل، لأنه أراد أن يخلق بعده أفضل منه

QURTUBI-FULL:19:7-8/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:19:7-8/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:19:7-8/r7.claim: The text favors noble, distinctive names because they are more memorable and less open to insulting nicknames; a poem and a genealogy anecdote illustrate this.
QURTUBI-FULL:19:7-8/r7.anchor: وفي هذه الآية دليل وشاهد على أن الأسامي السنع جديرة بالأثرة، وإياها كانت العرب تنتحي في التسمية لكونها أنبه وأنزه عن النبز

RAZI-FULL:v21p158#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p158#2/r1.speaker: الأكثرون
RAZI-FULL:v21p158#2/r1.claim: Most interpreters say God is the one calling to Zakariyyā, because the surrounding speech before and after is his address to God.
RAZI-FULL:v21p158#2/r1.anchor: فالأكثرون على أنه هو الله تعالى وذلك لأن ما قبل هذه الآية يدل

RAZI-FULL:v21p158#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p158#2/r2.speaker: آخرون
RAZI-FULL:v21p158#2/r2.claim: Others say an angel calls, citing the explicit account that the angels called while Zakariyyā prayed and the subsequent wording your Lord has said.
RAZI-FULL:v21p158#2/r2.anchor: فنادته الملئكة وهو قائم يصلى فى المحراب أن الله يبشرك بيحيى

RAZI-FULL:v21p158#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p158#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p158#2/r3.claim: The angel interpretation can be reconciled with the first view if both God and angels announced the glad tidings.
RAZI-FULL:v21p158#2/r3.anchor: يحتمل أن يقال حصل النداءان نداء الله ونداء الملائكة

RAZI-FULL:v21p158#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p158#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p158#2/r4.claim: The phrase your Lord has said in the next verse can itself be spoken by God, so it does not require an angel as speaker.

RAZI-FULL:v21p158#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p158#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p158#2/r5.claim: The apparent problem of either seeking a child without permission or receiving a redundant announcement has two answers: a personal request may be made without permission, or permission may have been given while its timing remained unknown.
RAZI-FULL:v21p158#2/r5.anchor: فيجوز أن يسأل بغير إذن ، ويحتمل أنه أذن له فيه ولم يعلم وقته

RAZI-FULL:v21p158#3/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p158#3/r1.speaker: ابن عباس والحسن وسعيد بن جبير وعكرمة وقتادة
RAZI-FULL:v21p158#3/r1.claim: They understand sami as a namesake: no one had previously been given the name Yaḥyā.
RAZI-FULL:v21p158#3/r1.anchor: وهو قول ابن عباس والحسن وسعيد بن جبير وعكرمة وقتادة أنه لم يسم أحد قبله بهذا الاسم

RAZI-FULL:v21p158#3/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p158#3/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p158#3/r2.claim: Another interpretation takes sami as an equal or counterpart, as in the later question whether one knows any equal to God.
RAZI-FULL:v21p158#3/r2.anchor: أن المراد بالسمي النظير كما في قوله : { هل تعلم له سميا }

RAZI-FULL:v21p158#3/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p158#3/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p158#3/r3.claim: One proposed counterpart is a prophet matching Yaḥyā in being masterly, chaste, and free from sin, echoing the request that God make him pleasing.
RAZI-FULL:v21p158#3/r3.anchor: أنه سيد وحصور لم يعص ولم يهم بمعصية كأنه جواب لقوله : { واجعله رب رضيا }

RAZI-FULL:v21p158#3/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p158#3/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p158#3/r4.claim: Al-Rāzī calls this weak because it would place Yaḥyā above earlier prophets such as Adam, Noah, Abraham, and Moses, contrary to consensus.
RAZI-FULL:v21p158#3/r4.anchor: وهذا الوجه ضعيف لأنه يقتضي تفضيله على الأنبياء الذين كانوا قبله

RAZI-FULL:v21p158#3/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p158#3/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p158#3/r5.claim: A further reading says God uniquely named Yaḥyā before he existed, whereas people normally receive names only after birth.
RAZI-FULL:v21p158#3/r5.anchor: فإن الله تعالى هو الذي سماه قبل دخوله في الوجود

RAZI-FULL:v21p158#3/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p158#3/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p158#3/r6.claim: Another explanation makes his unusual birth to an old man and infertile woman the unprecedented feature.
RAZI-FULL:v21p158#3/r6.anchor: أنه ولد بين شيخ فان وعجوز عاقر

RAZI-FULL:v21p158#3/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p158#3/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p158#3/r7.claim: Al-Rāzī prefers the literal namesake meaning because counterpart is a nonliteral shift without need; the context of worship in 19:65 requires that shift there, but not here, and a unique royal name honors its bearer.
RAZI-FULL:v21p158#3/r7.anchor: الوجه الأول أولى وذلك لأن حمل السمي على النظير وإن كان يفيد المدح

RAZI-FULL:v21p159/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p159/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
RAZI-FULL:v21p159/r1.claim: Al-Thaʿlabī transmits from Ibn ʿAbbās that Yaḥyā's name means God restored his mother's barrenness to fertility.
RAZI-FULL:v21p159/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما أن الله تعالى أحيا به عقر أمه

RAZI-FULL:v21p159/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p159/r2.speaker: قتادة
RAZI-FULL:v21p159/r2.claim: Qatāda says God made Yaḥyā's heart alive through faith and obedience, linking spiritual life to 6:122 and 8:24.
RAZI-FULL:v21p159/r2.anchor: عن قتادة أن الله تعالى أحيا قلبه بالإيمان والطاعة

RAZI-FULL:v21p159/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p159/r3.speaker: عكرمة عن ابن عباس عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
RAZI-FULL:v21p159/r3.claim: A report says everyone has sinned or intended to sin except Yaḥyā ibn Zakariyyā, who neither intended nor committed sin.
RAZI-FULL:v21p159/r3.anchor: ما من أحد إلا وقد عصى أو هم إلا يحيى بن زكريا

RAZI-FULL:v21p159/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p159/r4.speaker: أبو القاسم بن حبيب
RAZI-FULL:v21p159/r4.claim: Abū al-Qāsim ibn Ḥabīb says Yaḥyā was named for martyrdom, since martyrs are alive with their Lord.
RAZI-FULL:v21p159/r4.anchor: عن أبي القاسم بن حبيب أنه استشهد وأن الشهداء أحياء عند ربهم

RAZI-FULL:v21p159/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p159/r5.speaker: عمرو بن عبد الله المقدسي
RAZI-FULL:v21p159/r5.claim: ʿAmr ibn ʿAbd Allāh al-Maqdisī tells a naming story in which God calls Sarah to give a letter of her name to the servant Ḥayy, yielding Yaḥyā.
RAZI-FULL:v21p159/r5.anchor: أوحى الله تعالى إلى إبراهيم عليه السلام أن قل ليسارة

RAZI-FULL:v21p159/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p159/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p159/r6.claim: Another report says Yaḥyā first believed in Jesus: while their mothers were pregnant, the unborn Yaḥyā bowed to Jesus in Mary's womb.
RAZI-FULL:v21p159/r6.anchor: أن يحيى عليه السلام أول من آمن بعيسى فصار قلبه حيا بذلك الإيمان

RAZI-FULL:v21p159/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p159/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p159/r7.claim: A final explanation says religion itself comes alive through Yaḥyā, since Zakariyyā asked for him for religion's sake.
RAZI-FULL:v21p159/r7.anchor: أن الدين يحيا به لأنه إنما سأله زكريا لأجل الدين

RAZI-FULL:v21p159/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p159/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p159/r8.claim: Al-Rāzī judges these etymologies weak: proper names need not derive a descriptive meaning, but function as identifying signs.
RAZI-FULL:v21p159/r8.anchor: هذه الوجوه ضعيفة لأن أسماء الألقاب لا يطلب فيها وجه الاشتقاق

RAZI-FULL:v21p165#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p165#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p165#2/r3.claim: A supplicant should address God with the vocative “My Lord,” as Zachariah does here.
RAZI-FULL:v21p165#2/r3.anchor: أن يكون الدعاء بلفظ يا رب على ما في هذا الموضع

RAZI-FULL:v21p165#2/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p165#2/r10.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p165#2/r10.claim: Āl ʿImrān explicitly says the angels announced the news, while Maryam seems to make God the caller; Razi says both may have called, so there is no conflict.
RAZI-FULL:v21p165#2/r10.anchor: وفي هذه السورة الأظهر أن المنادي

STUDYQURAN:19:2/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:19:2/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:19:2/r1.claim: The linked stories of Mary, Zachariah, John, and Jesus show that divine creative power crosses ordinary physical limits.
STUDYQURAN:19:2/r1.anchor: The two stories are also connected in 21:89–91 as well as in the Biblical account found in Luke 1:5–80

STUDYQURAN:19:2/r20.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:19:2/r20.speaker: R, Ṭs
STUDYQURAN:19:2/r20.claim: The announcement may have come directly from God or through one or more angelic messengers.

STUDYQURAN:19:2/r21.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:19:2/r21.speaker: Ṭ
STUDYQURAN:19:2/r21.claim: Yaḥyā means “he lives” and may refer to Zachariah’s faith being brought to life.
STUDYQURAN:19:2/r21.anchor: it may refer to John’s having been brought to life through Zachariah’s faith (Ṭ)

STUDYQURAN:19:2/r22.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:19:2/r22.speaker: Bḍ
STUDYQURAN:19:2/r22.claim: The name may refer to John being miraculously brought to life in his mother’s womb.
STUDYQURAN:19:2/r22.anchor: his having been brought to life miraculously in his mother’s womb (Bḍ).

STUDYQURAN:19:2/r23.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:19:2/r23.speaker: R
STUDYQURAN:19:2/r23.claim: Another interpretation is that God enlivened John’s heart with faith and obedience.
STUDYQURAN:19:2/r23.anchor: God having enlivened his heart with faith and obedience (R).

STUDYQURAN:19:2/r24.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:19:2/r24.speaker: R, Ṭs
STUDYQURAN:19:2/r24.claim: God’s naming John before birth is a special honor; Jesus also receives his name from God.
STUDYQURAN:19:2/r24.anchor: That God Himself gives John his name is a distinct honor (R, Ṭs); Jesus is also given his name by God

STUDYQURAN:19:2/r25.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:19:2/r25.speaker: Ṭs
STUDYQURAN:19:2/r25.claim: The unprecedented name marks John’s special favor and virtue.
STUDYQURAN:19:2/r25.anchor: the special favor bestowed upon John, and his virtue (Ṭs;

STUDYQURAN:19:2/r26.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:19:2/r26.speaker: R
STUDYQURAN:19:2/r26.claim: The name’s uniqueness may reflect that God named John before birth, unlike children named by their parents afterward.
STUDYQURAN:19:2/r26.anchor: he was named by God Himself prior to his birth, while other children are named by their parents after they are born (R).

STUDYQURAN:19:2/r27.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:19:2/r27.speaker: Ṭs
STUDYQURAN:19:2/r27.claim: Shiite tradition links John’s unprecedented name and martyrdom to al-Ḥusayn’s name given by the Prophet and his martyrdom under Yazīd.
STUDYQURAN:19:2/r27.anchor: whose name, according to Shiite sources, was given by the Prophet himself and also had no precedent

NAHHAS:v3p7/r1.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p7/r1.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v3p7/r1.claim: يحيى is the predicate of اسمه, and indeclinable because it was originally an imperfect verb; its yāʾ spelling distinguishes it from the verb.
NAHHAS:v3p7/r1.anchor: ( اسمه يحيى ) مبتدأ وخبر ولم ينصرف يحيى لأنه في الأصل

NAHHAS:v3p7/r2.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p7/r2.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v3p7/r2.claim: One interpretation of سميا is that nobody before him had been commanded to name a son Yaḥyā.
NAHHAS:v3p7/r2.anchor: وقد قيل معناه لم نأمر أحدا أن يسمي ابنه يحيى قبلك

TAB-FULL:v15p461/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p461/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v15p461/r1.claim: God answers Zakariyyā by promising a boy named Yaḥyā.
TAB-FULL:v15p461/r1.anchor: حدثنا بشر، قال: ثنا يزيد، قال: ثنا سعيد، عن قتادة، قوله {يا زكريا إنا نبشرك بغلام اسمه يحيى}

TAB-FULL:v15p461/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p461/r2.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v15p461/r2.claim: God named Yaḥyā because He brought him to life through faith.
TAB-FULL:v15p461/r2.anchor: عن قتادة، قوله {يا زكريا إنا نبشرك بغلام اسمه يحيى} [مريم: 7] عبد أحياه الله للإيمان

TAB-FULL:v15p462/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p462/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v15p462/r1.claim: He interprets 'no namesake before him' to mean no barren woman had ever borne a child like Yaḥyā.
TAB-FULL:v15p462/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قوله ليحيى: {لم نجعل له من قبل سميا} [مريم: 7] يقول: لم تلد العواقر مثله ولدا قط

TAB-FULL:v15p462/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p462/r2.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v15p462/r2.claim: He interprets samiyyan as someone comparable or like him.
TAB-FULL:v15p462/r2.anchor: عن مجاهد، في قوله {لم نجعل له من قبل سميا} [مريم: 7] قال: شبيها

TAB-FULL:v15p462/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p462/r3.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v15p462/r3.claim: He says no one before Yaḥyā had been given that name.
TAB-FULL:v15p462/r3.anchor: عن قتادة، قوله: {لم نجعل له من قبل سميا} [مريم: 7] لم يسم به أحد قبله

TAB-FULL:v15p462/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p462/r4.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v15p462/r4.claim: He says no one before was named by this name.
TAB-FULL:v15p462/r4.anchor: قال: ثنا عبد الرحمن بن زيد بن أسلم، في قول الله: {لم نجعل له من قبل سميا} [مريم: 7]

TAB-FULL:v15p462/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p462/r5.speaker: السدي
TAB-FULL:v15p462/r5.claim: He says no one before Yaḥyā was named Yaḥyā.
TAB-FULL:v15p462/r5.anchor: عن السدي، {إنا نبشرك بغلام اسمه يحيى لم نجعل له من قبل سميا} [مريم: 7] لم يسم أحد قبله يحيى

TAB-FULL:v15p462/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v15p462/r6.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v15p462/r6.claim: He prefers the namesake interpretation: no one before Yaḥyā bore his name; samiyy is a form derived from the passive sense of naming.
TAB-FULL:v15p462/r6.anchor: قال أبو جعفر: وهذا القول أعني قول من قال: لم يكن ليحيى قبل يحيى أحد سمي باسمه أشبه بتأويل ذلك

TABATABAI:19:6-7/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:19:6-7/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:19:6-7/r1.claim: An alternative report says Zechariah saw Mary receive winter fruit in summer and summer fruit in winter, prompting him to hope God could grant him a child despite old age and barrenness.
TABATABAI:19:6-7/r1.anchor: فقد ورد في بعض الآثار أن زكريا كان يجد عند مريم فواكه في غير موسمها

TABATABAI:19:6-7/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:19:6-7/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:19:6-7/r3.claim: Even if the report is accepted, it explains hope for a child, followed by the request that the child be righteous and pleasing; inheritance marks the child and cannot mean nonhereditary spiritual stations without an unstated clue.
TABATABAI:19:6-7/r3.anchor: ولو سلم ذلك كان مقتضاه أن ينبعث زكريا بالقصد الأول إلى طلب الذرية والولد

TABATABAI:19:7-9/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:19:7-9/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:19:7-9/r1.claim: The announcement omits an abbreviated response, understood as We answered him and called: the parallel account says God granted Yahya.

TABATABAI:19:7-9/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:19:7-9/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:19:7-9/r2.claim: Al Imran says angels announced Yahya while Zechariah prayed, showing that the announcement was mediated by angels; the later wording your Lord said confirms this.
TABATABAI:19:7-9/r2.anchor: وتشهد آية آل عمران على أن قوله

TABATABAI:19:7-9/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:19:7-9/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:19:7-9/r3.claim: God named him Yahya, and no one before bore that same name; alternatively, samiyyan means an equal or counterpart, as in the later question whether anyone is God’s namesake.
TABATABAI:19:7-9/r3.anchor: وأنه لم يسم بهذا الأسم قبله أحد

TABATABAI:19:7-9/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:19:7-9/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:19:7-9/r4.claim: Yahya receives unique descriptions: wisdom as a child, leadership and chastity, and peace at birth, death, and resurrection; Jesus shared them but was born later, though they were cousins.
TABATABAI:19:7-9/r4.anchor: نعته في كلامه بنعوت لم ينعت به أحدا من أنبيائه وأوليائه قبله

TABATABAI:19:15/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:19:15/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:19:15/r7.claim: The Qur'an calls Zechariah prophet and recipient of revelation, servant, righteous, elect, and guided; it recounts his prayer for a child after witnessing Mary's worship and provision.
TABATABAI:19:15/r7.anchor: وصفه الله سبحانه في كلامه بالنبوة والوحي

TABATABAI:19:15/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:19:15/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:19:15/r8.claim: After Imran's death, Zechariah cared for Mary, found provision with her in the sanctuary, prayed for offspring despite old age and her barrenness, and received the promised John.
TABATABAI:19:15/r8.anchor: هنالك دعا زكريا ربه وسأله أن يهب له من امرأته ذرية طيبة

TABATABAI:19:15/r9.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:19:15/r9.speaker: author
TABATABAI:19:15/r9.claim: The angels announced John while Zechariah prayed; seeking reassurance, he received inability to speak for three days as a sign and gestured to his people to praise morning and evening.
TABATABAI:19:15/r9.anchor: فقيل له إن آيتك أن يعتقل لسانك فلا تكلم الناس ثلاثة أيام إلا رمزا

TABATABAI:19:1-15#6/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:19:1-15#6/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:19:1-15#6/r3.claim: The Qur'an praises John as affirming Jesus's prophethood, a leader, chaste, prophet, righteous, elect and guided; God named him uniquely, gave him wisdom as a child, and greeted him at the three stages.
TABATABAI:19:1-15#6/r3.anchor: كان مصدقا بكلمة من الله وهو تصديقه بنبوة المسيح

TABATABAI:19:1-15#7/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:19:1-15#7/r1.speaker: الإنجيل
TABATABAI:19:1-15#7/r1.claim: The Gospel introduces priest Zechariah and Aaronite Elizabeth as elderly, righteous, and childless; Gabriel announces John, who will abstain from wine, be filled with the Spirit, and prepare Israel in Elijah's spirit.
TABATABAI:19:1-15#7/r1.anchor: كان في أيام هيرودس ملك اليهودية كاهن اسمه زكريا

TABATABAI:19:1-15#7/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:19:1-15#7/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:19:1-15#7/r3.claim: The Gospel says Elizabeth gives birth; despite relatives' objection, she names the child John, Zechariah confirms the name in writing, regains speech, praises God, and prophesies.
TABATABAI:19:1-15#7/r3.anchor: فطلب لوحا وكتب قائلا اسمه يوحنا

TABRISI:19:7-11#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:19:7-11#2/r2.speaker: author
TABRISI:19:7-11#2/r2.claim: Ismuhu Yahya is a nominal clause modifying boy; kathalika has an omitted subject meaning the matter is as announced; lam tak drops its frequent final n.
TABRISI:19:7-11#2/r2.anchor: { اسمه يحيى } جملة اسمية مجرورة الموضع صفة الغلام

TABRISI:19:7-11#2/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:19:7-11#2/r5.speaker: قتادة وابن جريج والسدي وابن زيد
TABRISI:19:7-11#2/r5.claim: No one before Yahya had borne his name; the author calls this a distinction because God named him and chose a name not previously used.
TABRISI:19:7-11#2/r5.anchor: لم نجعل له من قبل سميا

TABRISI:19:7-11#2/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:19:7-11#2/r6.speaker: أبو عبد الله
TABRISI:19:7-11#2/r6.claim: He says Husayn too had no namesake; the sky was red at dawn and dusk for forty mornings, and the killers of Yahya and Husayn were illegitimate.
TABRISI:19:7-11#2/r6.anchor: لم يكن له من قبل سميا ولم تبك السماء إلا عليهما أربعين صباحا

TABRISI:19:7-11#2/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:19:7-11#2/r7.speaker: علي بن زيد عن علي بن الحسين
TABRISI:19:7-11#2/r7.claim: While travelling with Husayn, Ali Zayn al-Abidin says Husayn mentioned Yahya at every stop and recalled that Yahya’s head was presented to an adulteress.
TABRISI:19:7-11#2/r7.anchor: ما نزل منزلا ولا ارتحل منه إلا ذكر يحيى بن زكريا

THALABI:v6p207/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p207/r1.speaker: author
THALABI:v6p207/r1.claim: The announcement condenses the response to Zachariah's prayer: God promises a boy named Yahya.
THALABI:v6p207/r1.anchor: فيه إضمار واختصار، يعني فاستجاب دعاءه فقال: يا زكريا إنا نبشرك بغلام

THALABI:v6p207/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p207/r2.speaker: قتادة والكلبي
THALABI:v6p207/r2.claim: Qatada and al-Kalbi, with Ikrima's report from Ibn Abbas, say no one before Yahya bore that name.
THALABI:v6p207/r2.anchor: قال قتادة والكلبي: لم يسم أحد قبله يحيى، وهي رواية عكرمة عن ابن عباس،

THALABI:v6p207/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p207/r3.speaker: سعيد بن جبير وعطاء
THALABI:v6p207/r3.claim: Saeed ibn Jubayr and Ata interpret samiyyan as having no equal, as in 19:65; Mujahid transmits this from Ibn Abbas.
THALABI:v6p207/r3.anchor: وقال سعيد بن جبير وعطاء: لم نجعل له شبيها، ومثله دليله قوله تعالى هل تعلم له سميا

THALABI:v6p207/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p207/r4.speaker: author
THALABI:v6p207/r4.claim: On this view, Yahya had no equal because he never intended disobedience; one view also makes him unmatched among women because he was a master and celibate.
THALABI:v6p207/r4.anchor: وتأويل هذا القول أنه لم يكن له مثل لأنه لم يهم بمعصيته قط وقيل:

THALABI:v6p207/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p207/r5.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب عن ابن عباس
THALABI:v6p207/r5.claim: Ali reports Ibn Abbas's view that barren women had never borne a child like Yahya.
THALABI:v6p207/r5.anchor: وقال علي بن أبي طالب عن ابن عباس: لم تلد العواقر مثله ولدا،

THALABI:v6p207/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p207/r6.speaker: قيل
THALABI:v6p207/r6.claim: One interpretation says God qualified the claim with before because He intended to create someone greater afterward, Muhammad.
THALABI:v6p207/r6.anchor: وقيل: إن الله تعالى اشترط القبل لأنه جل ذكره أراد أن يخلق بعده من هو أفضل منه

THALABI:v6p207/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p207/r7.speaker: قيل
THALABI:v6p207/r7.claim: Other views limit the statement to some qualities, since it need not grant Yahya superiority in every respect and earlier patriarchs were greater.
THALABI:v6p207/r7.anchor: وقيل: إن الله تعالى لم يرد بهذا القول جميع الفضائل كلها ليحيى،

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p197#2/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p197#2/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p197#2/r1.claim: The text implies that God answered Zechariah’s prayer and gave glad tidings of Yaḥyā; the story was also discussed in Āl ʿImrān.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p197#2/r1.anchor: وقوله تعالى: {يا زكريا} فيه إضمار والمعنى: استجاب الله دعاءه فقال: {يا زكريا إنا نبشرك

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p197#2/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p197#2/r2.speaker: ابن عباس عن عكرمة وقتادة والكلبي وابن جريج والسدي وابن زيد والقتبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p197#2/r2.claim: They understand samiyyan as a name: no one before him was called Yaḥyā. God’s own naming distinguished him from children named by parents.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p197#2/r2.anchor: قال ابن عباس في رواية عكرمة: (لم يسم أحد قبله يحيى) (¬1). وهذا قول قتادة، والكلبي،

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p197#2/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p197#2/r3.speaker: الزجاج
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p197#2/r3.claim: He says Yaḥyā was named so because he was made alive through the knowledge and wisdom given him.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p197#2/r3.anchor: قال الزجاج: (قيل: سمي يحيى؛ لأنه حيي بالعلم والحكمة التي أوتيها)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p197#2/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p197#2/r4.speaker: ابن عباس عن عطاء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p197#2/r4.claim: He explains samiyyan as someone with no counterpart in God’s prior knowledge.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p197#2/r4.anchor: وقال ابن عباس في رواية عطاء: {لم نجعل له من قبل سميا} يريد: (لم يكن له في سابق علمي نظير

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p197#2/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p197#2/r5.speaker: ابن عباس عن الوالبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p197#2/r5.claim: He says no barren woman had previously borne a child like him.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p197#2/r5.anchor: وقال في رواية الوالبي: (لم تلد العواقر مثله ولدا)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p197#2/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p197#2/r6.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p197#2/r6.claim: Saʿīd ibn Jubayr glosses samiyyan as equal or peer.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p197#2/r6.anchor: وهذا قول سعيد بن جبير: {لم نجعل له من قبل سميا} قال: (عدلا)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p197#2/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p197#2/r7.speaker: مجاهد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p197#2/r7.claim: Mujāhid glosses it as a likeness or counterpart.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p197#2/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p197#2/r8.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p197#2/r8.claim: On the counterpart reading, compare 19:65; Yaḥyā had no human peer because he never sinned or intended sin.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p197#2/r8.anchor: وعلى هذا القول فالمراد بالسمي: المثل والنظير كقوله: {هل تعلم له سميا} [مريم: 65]،

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:19:5-8/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:19:5-8/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:19:5-8/r4.claim: God answered Zechariah and announced a boy named Yahya because he would live through knowledge and obedience; no one before him had that name.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:19:5-8/r4.anchor: يا زكريا إنا نبشرك بغلام } ولد ذكر { اسمه يحيى } لأنه يحيا بالعلم والطاعة { لم نجعل له من قبل سميا } لم يسم أحد قبله بهذا الاسم،

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p214#2/r5.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p214#2/r5.speaker: قتادة
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p214#2/r5.claim: Qatāda says God brought Yahya to life through faith.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p214#2/r5.anchor: سعيد، عن قتادة قال: أحياه الله بالإيمان.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p214#2/r6.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p214#2/r6.speaker: قتادة
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p214#2/r6.claim: Qatāda explains “no namesake before him” to mean no one before Yahya had been given that name.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p214#2/r6.anchor: سعيد، عن قتادة قال: لم يسم به أحدا قبله، يعني يحيى.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p214#2/r7.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p214#2/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p214#2/r7.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says no barren woman had given birth before him; samiyyan means one comparable to him.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p214#2/r7.anchor: وبلغني عن ابن عباس قال: لم تلد العواقر قبله يقول: {سميا} [مريم: 7] ، يساميه

ELMALILI:19:1-15/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:19:1-15/r6.speaker: author
ELMALILI:19:1-15/r6.claim: One possible symbolic reading maps Kāf to Zechariah, Hā to his wife, Yā to John, ʿAyn to Jesus, and Ṣād to Mustafa, summarizing the sura.
ELMALILI:19:1-15/r6.anchor: kâf Zekeriyyâ’ya, hâ zevcesine, yâ Yahyâ’ya, ayn Îsâ’ya, sad Mustafa’ya remz olarak sûrenin mazmûnunu bir icmal olmak muhtemil

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:19:7/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:19:7/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:19:7/r1.claim: God accepted Zakariya's prayer and announced Yahya's birth, as also noted at 21:90.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:19:7/r1.anchor: Yüce Allah, Hz. Zekeriyyâ’nın duasını kabul etti ve Yahyâ adında bir oğlunun olacağını ona müjdeledi

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:19:7/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:19:7/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:19:7/r2.claim: Samiyy can mean named or similar; commentators prefer named because calling Yahya unmatched would imply superiority to earlier great prophets such as Abraham and Moses.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:19:7/r2.anchor: Tefsirciler, böyle bir anlayış Yahyâ’nın, kendisinden önceki Hz. İbrâhim ve Hz. Mûsâ gibi büyük peygamberlerden de üstün olmasını gerektireceği için birinci mânayı tercih etmişlerdir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:19:7/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:19:7/r3.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:19:7/r3.claim: No earlier prophet combined Yahya's traits: birth to elderly parents, his unprecedented name, and wisdom in childhood, understood as prophethood or grasp of scripture.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:19:7/r3.anchor: onun ihtiyar bir baba ile kısır ve yaşlı bir anneden dünyaya gelmesi, Yahyâ adının ondan önce hiç kimseye verilmemiş olması

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:19:7/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:19:7/r4.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:19:7/r4.claim: Yahya was also called master and prophet, specially guarded in chastity, ascetic, and herald of Jesus' mission; these distinctions do not make him absolutely the greatest prophet.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:19:7/r4.anchor: bu meziyetler onun mutlak mânada en üstün peygamber olduğunu değil, anılan niteliklerden dolayı farklı olduğunu ifade eder

SAMIN-DURR:19:7/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:19:7/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:19:7/r1.claim: The apparent view is that Yaḥyā is a foreign proper name with no derivation, hence diptote for properness and foreignness.
SAMIN-DURR:19:7/r1.anchor: فيه قولان: أحدهما: أنه سام أعجمي لا اشتقاق له، وهذا هو الظاهر، ومنعه من الصرف للعلمية والعجمة

SAMIN-DURR:19:7/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:19:7/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:19:7/r2.claim: Alternatively, Yaḥyā was transferred from a present-tense verb, like the names Yaʿmar, Yaʿīsh, and Yamut ibn al-Muzarriʿ.
SAMIN-DURR:19:7/r2.anchor: وقيل: بل هو منقول من الفعل المضارع كما سموا بيعمر ويعيش ويموت، وهو يموت بن المزرع

SAMIN-DURR:19:7/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:19:7/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:19:7/r3.claim: Both ismuhu Yaḥyā and lam najʿal form genitive adjectival clauses describing ghulām.
SAMIN-DURR:19:7/r3.anchor: والجملة من قوله: { اسمه يحيى } في محل جر صفة ل " غلام " وكذلك { لم نجعل }

SAMIN-DURR:19:7/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:19:7/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:19:7/r4.claim: Samiyyan follows the morphology of raḍiyyan and derives from sumuww (‘elevation’), supporting the Basran derivation of ism from sumuww; if from wasm, one would say wasīman.
SAMIN-DURR:19:7/r4.anchor: و " سميا " كقوله: " رضيا " إعرابا وتصريفا لأنه من السمو، وفيه دلالة لقول البصريين: أن الاسم من السمو

ZAJJAJ:v3p320/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p320/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
ZAJJAJ:v3p320/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas says no one had previously been named Yaḥyā.

ZAJJAJ:v3p320/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p320/r3.speaker: قيل
ZAJJAJ:v3p320/r3.claim: Another explanation says he was named Yaḥyā because he was enlivened by the knowledge and wisdom given to him.
ZAJJAJ:v3p320/r3.anchor:
وقيل سمي بيحيى
لأنه حيى بالعلم وبالحكمة التي أوتيها،

ZAJJAJ:v3p320/r4.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p320/r4.speaker: قيل
ZAJJAJ:v3p320/r4.claim: A third explanation takes samiyyan to mean an equal or counterpart.
ZAJJAJ:v3p320/r4.anchor:
وقيل لم نجعل له من قبل سميا، أي
نظيرا ومثلا.

ASAD-NOTES:19:7#n7/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:19:7#n7/r1.speaker: Asad
ASAD-NOTES:19:7#n7/r1.claim: Yahya means "he shall live": John will be spiritually alive and remembered forever.
ASAD-NOTES:19:7#n7/r1.anchor: The name Yahya (John) signifies "he shall live", i.e., he will be spiritually alive and will be remembered forever

ASAD-NOTES:19:7#n7/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:19:7#n7/r2.speaker: Asad
ASAD-NOTES:19:7#n7/r2.claim: God's choice of the name was a singular distinction and a divine promise, as discussed in the note on 3:39.
ASAD-NOTES:19:7#n7/r2.anchor: the fact that God Himself had chosen this name for him was a singular distinction, equivalent to a divine promise

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: The prophets in Adam’s, Noah’s, and Abraham’s lines preached monotheism, prayer, and zakāh, but their followers turned to polytheism, abandoned the rites, and followed innovations and desires.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: all celebrated prophets born in the progeny of Adam (sws), Noah (sws) and Abraham (sws) preached monotheism.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: The Prophet is urged to persevere against their hostility and is given glad tidings of success.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: the Prophet (sws) is urged to show perseverance on their attitude and given glad tidings of success.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: The adversaries mistake worldly success for proof of their truth; it is only respite until the truth is conclusively conveyed and they have no excuse when seized.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: they regard their worldly successes in contrast to the believers to be a reason of their own veracity.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: Jesus and Mary are prominent because Christians and Jews secretly supported Quraysh; the Qur’an exposes the People of the Book to show they cannot support a truthless cause.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: the Christians too had begun to secretly support the Quraysh.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: The Zacharias story introduces Mary’s story and counters Christians who treat Jesus’s miraculous birth as proof of his divinity.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: This incident forms a prelude to the anecdote of Mary (sws) mentioned subsequently.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: A sincere supplication with the right timing, objective, feelings, and wording is accepted; God can bring mercy despite apparently hopeless circumstances.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: When a supplication is made at the right time, with the correct objective, with sincere emotions and with the right selection of words, it is immediately accepted.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: The word samiyy means a peer or example; God assures Zachariah that his child will have no parallel despite the parents' age and barrenness.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: These words are meant to assure Zacharias (sws) that though he has become old and his wife is barren

IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p236/r3.author: Ibn Khālawayh (attr.)
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p236/r3.speaker: author
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p236/r3.claim: The name Yaḥyā is explained as God bringing life from two infertile parents who had passed ninety and despaired of having a child.
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p236/r3.anchor: وإنما سمي يحيى لأنه حيي من عقمين قد نيفا على التسعين ويئسا من الولد

IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p236/r4.author: Ibn Khālawayh (attr.)
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p236/r4.speaker: author
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p236/r4.claim: Samiyyan may mean no one before bore the same name, or that no child had been born to his parents before him; the later question about a namesake allows both senses.
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p236/r4.anchor: قيل لم يسم باسمه غيره وقيل لم يولد لأبويه ولد قبله

QIRAAT-ER:19:7:2#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:19:7:2#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:19:7:2#1/r1.claim: Adding hamza to Zakariyyā supplies nominative case inflection and links the name continuously to innā.
QIRAAT-ER:19:7:2#1/r1.anchor: Hamza added at end of Zakariyyā (Zakariyyāʾu), giving it case inflection (nominative)

QIRAAT-ER:19:7:2#2/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:19:7:2#2/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:19:7:2#2/r1.claim: The same hamza addition is paired with a marked pause or phonological break before innā.
QIRAAT-ER:19:7:2#2/r1.anchor: Same hamza addition; •اِنَّا shows a deliberate pause or phonological break before innā

QIRAAT-ER:19:7:4#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:19:7:4#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:19:7:4#1/r1.claim: Form I nabshuru replaces Form II nubashshiru, reducing the verb to a simpler form rather than an intensive heralding.
QIRAAT-ER:19:7:4#1/r1.anchor: Form I (nabshuru) instead of Form II (nubashshiru): verb form reduced — simpler

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p4/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p4/r1.speaker: قتادة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p4/r1.claim: Qatada says no one before Yahya had borne that name.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p4/r1.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله تعالى ﴿ لم نجعل له من قبل سميا ﴾ قال لم يسم أحد قبله يحيى

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p237/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p237/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p237/r1.claim: The surah is Meccan like the previous one; Muqatil exempts the prostration verse, saying it was revealed in Medina after the migration to Abyssinia.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p237/r1.anchor: هذه السورة مكية كالسورة التي قبلها. وقال مقاتل: إلا آية

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p237/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p237/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p237/r2.claim: The surahs connect through astonishing stories: the earlier tells of the Cave, Moses and Khidr, and Dhul-Qarnayn; this one of John’s birth to an old man and barren woman and Jesus’ birth without a father.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p237/r2.anchor: ومناسبتها لما قبلها أنه تعالى ضمن السورة قبلها قصصا عجبا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p242/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p242/r1.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p242/r1.claim: The call came immediately after Zakariyya's supplication; other reports say the child came forty or sixty years later.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p242/r1.anchor: وقيل: رزقه بعد أربعين سنة من دعائه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p242/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p242/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p242/r2.claim: The callers and bearers of good news were angels, sent by God's revelation, as in the account of the angels calling.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p242/r2.anchor: والمنادي والمبشر زكرياء هم الملائكة بوحي من الله تعالى قال تعالى فنادته الملائكة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p242/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p242/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p242/r3.claim: Ghulām denotes a male child; the related feminine ghulāma is also used.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p242/r3.anchor: والغلام الولد الذكر، وقد يقال للأثني غلامة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p242/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p242/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p242/r4.claim: Yaḥyā is apparently a non-Arabic name; if Arabic, it would be a verb-name like Yaʿmar or Yaʿīsh, and Arabs even named someone Yamūt.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p242/r4.anchor: والظاهر أن يحيى ليس عربيا لأنه لم تكن عادتهم أن يسموا بألفاظ العربية

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p242/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p242/r5.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p242/r5.claim: One proposed etymology says he is named Yaḥyā because he lives by wisdom and chastity.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p242/r5.anchor: سمي بذلك لأنه يحيى بالحكمة والعفة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p242/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p242/r6.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p242/r6.claim: Another etymology says his guidance revives the many people he guides.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p242/r6.anchor: وقيل: يحيي بهدايته وإشادة خلق كثير

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p242/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p242/r7.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p242/r7.claim: Another etymology links his name to martyrdom, because martyrs are alive.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p242/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p242/r8.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p242/r8.claim: Other proposed meanings are that he lives a long time or is born alive despite his elderly father and barren mother.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p242/r8.anchor: وقيل: لأنه يعمر زمنا طويلا. وقيل: لأنه حيي بين شيخ كبير وأم عاقر
