ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p242/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p242/r9.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p242/r9.claim: A further etymology says his conception revived his mother's barren womb.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p242/r9.anchor: وقيل: لأنه حيي به عقر أمه وكانت لا تلد

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p242/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p242/r10.speaker: ابن عباس وقتادة والسدي وابن أسلم
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p242/r10.claim: They say no one before him had been named Yaḥyā.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p242/r10.anchor: وقال ابن عباس وقتادة والسدي وابن أسلم: لم نسم قبله أحدا بيحيى

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p242/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p242/r11.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p242/r11.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī says rare and striking names deserve distinction and were favored by Arabs as conspicuous and free of ordinary naming.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p242/r11.anchor: وهذا شاهد على أن الأسامي الشنع جديرة بالأثرة وإياها كانت العرب تنحي في التسمية

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p242/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p242/r12.speaker: رؤبة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p242/r12.claim: Ruʾba's verse praises people with striking names, using shanaʿ as evidence for unusual naming.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p242/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p242/r13.speaker: رؤبة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p242/r13.claim: Ruʾba answered the genealogist al-Bakrī that he was the son of al-ʿAjjāj, and the latter said he had recognized his lineage.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p242/r13.anchor: وقال رؤبة للنسابة البكري: وقد سأله عن نسبه أنا ابن العجاج

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p242/r14.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p242/r14.speaker: الصلت بن عطاء
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p242/r14.claim: Al-Ṣalt ibn ʿAṭāʾ said his unusual name, along with exile and caution, helped him advance among the Barmakids.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p242/r14.anchor: وقيل للصلت بن عطاء: كيف تقدمت عند البرامكة وعندهم من هو آدب منك، فقال: كنت غريب الدار غريب الاسم خفيف الحزم شحيحا بالأشلاء

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p242/r15.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p242/r15.speaker: مجاهد وغيره
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p242/r15.claim: They interpret samiyyan as an equal or counterpart, from the root of elevation and naming.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p242/r15.anchor: وقال مجاهد وغيره سميا أي مثلا ونظيرا وكأنه من المساماة والسمو

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p242/r16.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p242/r16.speaker: ابن عطية
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p242/r16.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya finds that interpretation far-fetched because Yaḥyā was not superior to Abraham and Moses.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p242/r16.anchor: قال ابن عطية: وهذا فيه بعد لأنه لا يفضل على إبراهيم وموسى

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p242/r17.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p242/r17.speaker: ابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p242/r17.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās also says no barren woman gave birth to anyone like Yaḥyā.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p242/r17.anchor: وقال ابن عباس أيضا لم تلد العواقر مثله

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p242/r18.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p242/r18.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p242/r18.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī explains that two similar people each become the other's namesake, like a match, peer, or counterpart.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p242/r18.anchor: كل متشاكلين يسمى كل واحد منهما باسم المثل والشبيه والشكل والنظير

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p242/r19.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p242/r19.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p242/r19.claim: Another view says he had no equal because he never disobeyed or even intended sin, was born to aged and barren parents, and was celibate.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p242/r19.anchor: لم يكن له مثل في أنه لم يعص ولم يهم بمعصية قط

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالهمز)#649/f17.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالهمز)#649/f17.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالهمز)#649/f17.claim: Sībawayh reports a recitation softening the first hamza and fully realizing the second, and attributes this pattern to Abū ʿAmr.

SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالهمز)#649/f20.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالهمز)#649/f20.speaker: العرب
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالهمز)#649/f20.claim: Other Arabs fully realize the first hamza and soften the second; Sībawayh heard this from trusted speakers.
SIBAWAYH:(هذابابالهمز)#649/f20.anchor: سمعنا ذلك من العرب وهو قولك

BURHAN:v2p380/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p380/r2.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p380/r2.claim: The author groups لم نجعل له من قبل سميا with Quranic statements about what God did not make, alongside examples framed with ما جعل; he says these patterns distinguish whether renewal of the stated matter is expected.
BURHAN:v2p380/r2.anchor: في جميع مواضع ما حصل المذكور أمورا لا يتوقع تجددها

BURHAN:v2p380/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p380/r3.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p380/r3.claim: Zarkashi presents Quranic rhetorical styles as the book’s chief aim because they disclose the secrets of the Quran’s inimitable composition, arrangement, sweetness, and fluency.
BURHAN:v2p380/r3.anchor: وهو المقصود الأعظم من هذا الكتاب وهو بيت القصيدة وأول الجريدة وغرة الكتيبة

ITQAN:v4p370#2/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p370#2/r1.speaker: عمرو بن مرة
ITQAN:v4p370#2/r1.claim: Ibn Abi Hatim transmits from ʿAmr ibn Murrah that five people were named before birth: Muhammad/Ahmad, Yahya, Jesus, Isaac, and Jacob.
ITQAN:v4p370#2/r1.anchor: أخرج ابن أبي حاتم عن عمرو بن مرة قال خمسة سموا قبل أن يكونوا

ITQAN:v4p370#2/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p370#2/r2.speaker: الراغب
ITQAN:v4p370#2/r2.claim: Al-Raghib says the name Ahmad in Jesus’ prophecy signals that Muhammad is more praiseworthy than Jesus and those before him.
ITQAN:v4p370#2/r2.anchor: قال الراغب وخص لفظ ( أحمد ) فيما بشر به عيسى تنبيها على أنه أحمد منه ومن الذين قبله

DAMGHANI:v1p246/r7.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p246/r7.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p246/r7.claim: Ism can mean the act or designation of naming; “his name is Yaḥyā” means his naming.
DAMGHANI:v1p246/r7.anchor: الرابع : الأسماء يعني التسميات فذلك قوله تعالى في سورة مريم

DAMGHANI:v1p246/r10.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p246/r10.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p246/r10.claim: For Yaḥyā, samiyyan is glossed as a son previously named Yaḥyā.
DAMGHANI:v1p246/r10.anchor: يعني عديلا ومثلا كقوله تعالى ( فيها )

DAMGHANI:v1p340/r16.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p340/r16.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p340/r16.claim: Ghulām refers to Yaḥyā ibn Zakariyyā, the boy whose birth is announced to Zachariah.
DAMGHANI:v1p340/r16.anchor: الغلام يريد به يحيى بن زكريا

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p560/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p560/r2.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p560/r2.claim: Bint al-Shati notes that although the Qur'an uses walad and awlād forty-six times, she finds no reading of samiyy as son in either Maryam verse.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p560/r2.anchor: ولم اقف على تأويل "سميا" بولد، في آيتى مريم، كلتيهما

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p560/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p560/r3.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p560/r3.claim: In Arabic, one's samiyy is a namesake or counterpart; the related verbs can mean matching or competing, while simah is a mark and ism a distinguishing name.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p560/r3.anchor: سَمِيُّكَ في اللغة: مَن اسمُه اسمُك ونظيرُك. وساماه باراه، وتساموا تباروا. والسمة العلامة

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p561/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p561/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p561/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas explains the phrase as meaning that no barren woman had previously borne a child like Yahya.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p561/r1.anchor: لم تلد العواقر مثله، عن ابن عباس

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p561/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p561/r2.speaker: آخرون
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p561/r2.claim: Other interpreters take it to mean that no likeness had previously been made for Yahya.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p561/r2.anchor: وقال آخرون: لم نجعل له من قبله مثلا

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p561/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p561/r3.speaker: الطبري
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p561/r3.claim: A further view says no one had borne Yahya’s name before; al-Tabari regards this as the closest interpretation.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p561/r3.anchor: وقال غيرهم: بل معناه أنه لم يسمَّ باسمه أحد قبله. وهذا القول الأخير، هو أشبه بتأويلها عند الطبري

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p792/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p792/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p792/r1.claim: The announcement in Al ʿImrān gives John more and fuller attributes than the brief announcement in Maryam; the greater detail shapes the differences that follow.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p792/r1.anchor: كان التفصيل بالصفات الكاملة في سورة آل عمران ليحيى أكثر منها في سورة مريم

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p792/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p792/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p792/r2.claim: A greater glad tiding calls for greater thanks: Al ʿImrān specifies three days of silence, when the sign and remembrance are clearer than at night, while Maryam specifies three nights.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p792/r2.anchor: الذكر في الليل أقل منه في النهار والآية أظهر وأبين

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p792/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p792/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p792/r3.claim: In Al ʿImrān God tells Zechariah to remember and praise Him himself; in Maryam Zechariah asks his people to praise, and his own praise would show gratitude more directly.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p792/r3.anchor: وتسبيح زكريا أدلّ على شكره لله تعالى من تسبيح قوم زكريا

NASHR:v1p387/r3.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p387/r3.speaker: نافع
NASHR:v1p387/r3.claim: Nafi’s reading is the one involved in five disputed Prophet-address loci; the disputed Maryam form is excepted for Hamza, al-Kisai, Khalaf, and Hafs.

NASHR:v2p239/r7.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p239/r7.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p239/r7.claim: Hamza and al-Kisa'i use the light form from بشر in the two occurrences here and the listed occurrences in al-Isra, al-Kahf, al-Tawbah, al-Hijr, and Maryam; the others use the doubled form from بشر, suggesting intensified giving of glad tidings.
NASHR:v2p239/r7.anchor: فقرأ حمزة والكسائي، يبشرك في الموضعين هنا ويبشر في سبحان والكهف

BURHAN:v2p211/r6.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p211/r6.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p211/r6.claim: The source lists these phrases as examples of rare or unusual Quranic vocabulary treated in works on غريب القرآن.
